distractors: Made more complicated than the problem requires, usually by someone enjoying the design more than the outcome.
Put together quickly out of whatever was to hand, holding up well enough for now and never meant to survive contact with a second user.

Kept deliberately vague so that nobody can be held to it later, which is a choice about exposure rather than a failure of drafting. It shows up first in the dates and in the numbers that never quite appear.

Copied closely from an existing example without the reasoning behind it being carried across, so that the shape is right and the fit is wrong. It survives review because everyone recognises the pattern and nobody checks whether it applies here.

Technically correct and completely beside the point, answering a question nobody in the room had asked. It is the most frustrating kind of contribution precisely because there is nothing in it to argue with, and it costs ten minutes the meeting did not have to spend.
